items.actClause:
AN ACT to require the department of environmental conservation to report on
coyote management techniques in urban and suburban areas
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S2100

SPONSOR: MAYER
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to require the department of environmental conservation to report
on coyote management techniques in urban and suburban areas

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

The purpose of this bill is to commission the department of environ-
mental conservation to provide a report to the legislature regarding
coyote management techniques in urban and suburban areas in order to
improve practices and safety of residents.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of this bill specifies that the coyote management report must
include: management measures currently taken, a review of effective
measures in other states, tools to enhance public engagement, identifi-
cation and evaluation of areas in the state with high concentrations of
coyotes, current and recommended methods for minimizing dangerous coyote
and human interactions, the rationales for current coyote population
management levels, and an evaluation of alternative coyote population
control methods.

Section 2 establishes the effective date.

 
DIFFERENCE BETWEEN ORIGINAL AND AMENDED VERSION (IF APPLICABLE):

None

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The surging population of coyotes, a heretofore largely unseen predator
in New York State, has alarmed many residents. A report designed to
illuminate current coyote management issues, best practices, and options
for handling future problems is a positive, practical step toward
resolving the issue.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2017: A8626 (Mayer)
2018: S8571

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

items.memoText:
VETO MESSAGE - No. 159
 
TO THE SENATE:
 
I am returning herewith, without my approval, the following bill:
 
Senate Bill Number 2100-B, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT  to require the department of environmental conservation to
      report on coyote  management  techniques  in  urban  and  suburban
      areas"
 
    NOT APPROVED
 
  This  bill  would  direct the Department of Environmental Conservation
(DEC) to provide a report, by January 1, 2022, of existing and potential
coyote management techniques for urban and suburban areas in the  State.
DEC  is  already  actively  involved  in  educating the public on coyote
management techniques that  are  designed  to  avoid  human  and  coyote
conflicts.  DEC  provides  direct  outreach  to municipalities on coyote
management and engages with local communities to help the public  under-
stand  coyote ecology and find ways to minimize risk to people and pets.
In that regard, many of the bill's goals have already been met.
 
  In the event of an incident, DEC  also  maintains  a  Coyote  Incident
Standard  Operating Procedure used by staff in the event of an incident,
which goes further than the study that would be required by the bill  by
providing  staff with instructions on how to address incidents once they
happen. In addition to the information already made  available  by  DEC,
there  are  several  other state, federal, and private publications that
already survey available coyote management techniques. Requiring DEC  to
recreate  a  study  would  not  be a meaningful exercise in light of the
amount of information already available on coyote management.
 
  Since the information sought by the bill is already available and  DEC
staff  is already actively engaged in public education of coyote related
issues, it is unnecessary to have DEC expend  significant  resources  to
identify  techniques already in use around the State. For these reasons,
I must veto this bill.
 
  The bill is disapproved.                    (signed) ANDREW M. CUOMO
 
                               __________
